tasks.title: Explain a delayed journey
tasks.objective: Understand a short disruption narrative and communicate an updated plan with consistent times.
tasks.context:
Hier, Lina devait rejoindre une amie à Tours. À la gare, elle a appris que son train avait vingt minutes de retard. Elle a envoyé un message : « Je suis encore à la gare. Ne m’attends pas devant le cinéma ; retrouve-moi au café à dix-huit heures. » Finalement, le train est parti avec dix minutes de retard seulement. Lina est arrivée avant l’heure proposée, mais elle n’a pas changé le rendez-vous.

Understand: Track the original delay, the actual delay and the new meeting arrangement separately. Devait presents an earlier plan; a appris and a envoyé move the story forward. Finalement signals the outcome, not necessarily a late arrival at the meeting.

Language: Use a simple past event to explain a change and a clear present instruction for the current arrangement. Do not treat every past event as background.

tasks.title: Transfer and review: Explain a delayed journey
tasks.objective: Understand a short disruption narrative and communicate an updated plan with consistent times.
tasks.context:
Write 70–90 French words to a friend: explain an invented transport delay, distinguish the announced and actual problem, and propose a place and time. Add one clarification question. Check the sequence and reread all times.

Speaking transfer: Explain a delayed journey to the Tutor as your friend. Confirm the new place and time and answer a follow-up question.

Revision: Retell the events in three steps without the text, then compare the actual delay and appointment details.

Self-review: check task fulfilment, evidence, sequence, grammar and spelling. Save a revised version after feedback. AI feedback is advisory; this module check is not a calibrated diagnostic or CEFR level-end examination.
